How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
IP: 192.120.45.67
API name: get information of an interface
Parameter_fabricName: Network1
Parameter_nodeId: 12
Parameter_podId: 10
Parameter_interfaceType: Ethernet
Parameter_infoType: Speed

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Send a GET request to retrieve specified information for an interface from a network telemetry API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL endpoint to send the GET request to. This should include the base path without query parameters, e.g., 'https://{ip}/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo'.

params.description: The query parameters for the request.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric to limit nodes pertaining to.

nodeId.description: The node identifier to limit results pertaining to.

podId.description: The pod identifier to limit results pertaining to.

interfaceType.description: The type of the interface to limit results pertaining to.

infoType.description: The type of information requested for the interface.

message.content:
Below is a step‑by‑step guide to build and send a **RESTful GET** request to the Cisco Nexus Dashboard (ND) API that returns the *Speed* information for a specific interface. | Item | Value | |------|-------| | **Base URL** | `https://192.120.45.67` | | **Endpoint** | `/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo` | | **HTTP Method** | `GET` | | **Query Parameters** | `fabricName=Network1`
`nodeId=12`
`podId=10`
`interfaceType=ethernet`
`infoType=Speed` | | **Headers** | `Authorization: Bearer `
`Accept: application/json` | --- ## 1. Build the full URL ```text https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo?fabricName=Network1&nodeId=12&podId=10&interfaceType=ethernet&infoType=Speed ``` > **Tip:** > * `interfaceType` is case‑sensitive and must match one of the allowed values (`gigabitethernet`, `fastethernet`, `ethernet`, `serial`). > * `infoType` can be `statistics`, `status`, `config`, or `Speed`. --- ## 2. Example `curl` command ```bash curl -k \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN" \ -H "Accept: application/json" \ "https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo?fabricName=Network1&nodeId=12&podId=10&interfaceType=ethernet&infoType=Speed" ``` * `-k` – skip certificate verification (use only in test environments). * Replace `YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN` with the token you obtained from ND. --- ## 3. Example in Python (`requests`) ```python import requests url = "https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo" params = { "fabricName": "Network1", "nodeId": 12, "podId": 10, "interfaceType": "ethernet", "infoType": "Speed" } headers = { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN", "Accept": "application/json" } response = requests.get(url, params=params, headers=headers, verify=False) print(response.status_code) print(response.json()) ``` --- ## 4. Using the provided `functions.requests_get` helper If you want to invoke the helper directly (e.g., inside a script that already imports the `functions` namespace): ```python from functions import requests_get result = requests_get( url="https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo", params={ "fabricName": "Network1", "nodeId": 12, "podId": 10, "interfaceType": "ethernet", "infoType": "Speed" } ) print(result) # <-- JSON payload returned by ND ``` > **Note:** > The helper will automatically handle the HTTP request; you still need to supply a valid bearer token via the environment or a global header configuration if the helper expects it. --- ## 5. What to expect in the response A successful call will return a JSON object similar to: ```json { "fabricName": "Network1", "nodeId": 12, "podId": 10, "interfaceType": "ethernet", "infoType": "Speed", "speed": "1000Mbps" } ``` If the interface does not exist or the parameters are wrong, you’ll receive an error code (e.g., `404 Not Found` or `400 Bad Request`) with a descriptive message. --- ### Quick Checklist | ✅ | Item | |----|------| | ✅ | Correct base URL (`https://192.120.45.67`) | | ✅ | Correct endpoint (`/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo`) | | ✅ | Proper query parameters (`fabricName`, `nodeId`, `podId`, `interfaceType`, `infoType`) | | ✅ | Valid bearer token in `Authorization` header | | ✅ | `Accept: application/json` header | | ✅ | HTTPS (verify SSL or use `-k`/`verify=False` for testing) | Follow the steps above and you’ll have a working RESTful API request to fetch the interface speed from Cisco Nexus Dashboard. Happy querying!
